proposals.announcement_evidence: production of the Modular Fuel System - Tank Rack Module
proposals.rationale: The award is a firm-fixed-price production contract for the Modular Fuel System Tank Rack Module, the fuel-distribution item that BLI 4700MA6000 (Distribution Systems, Petroleum & Water) buys and whose narrative owns the name 'The Modular Fuel System (MFS)'. Two other lines carry an MFS name: 1110MA4500 (Modification Of In-Svc Equipment, OPA-3) and 0604804A (RDT&E, and only for the M107 40gpm pump modification kit). The announcement's own word 'production' is the discriminator: this is new-build end items, not a modification of fielded equipment and not an engineering-development kit, so the procurement line that buys the MFS is the one whose own work this action pays for.

refute_a.reason: Production of MFS Tank Rack Modules is a procurement action and 4700MA6000's own narrative carries the TRM with an Army Acquisition Objective ('AAO: 114 ... The Modular Fuel System (MFS) Tank Rack Module (TRM) is a 2,500 gallon mobile storage'), so the procured end item is this OPA line's own buy, not a platform it supports; 'Distribution Systems, Petroleum & Water' is a six-system family line, not a CATCHALL_TITLE aggregate.

refute_b.reason: Name collision is total: BLI 1110MA4500 owns the byte-identical string 'The Modular Fuel System (MFS)' in the same lexicon doc 346, and 0604804A owns the only index row containing the announcement's own words 'Tank Rack Module'; the order names no appropriation ('funding will be determined with each order'), so nothing in the evidence picks 4700MA6000 over the other two owners.

proposals.announcement_evidence: The Personnel Recovery Support System Personnel Recovery Device
proposals.rationale: The announcement names the Personnel Recovery Support System verbatim and buys its Personnel Recovery Device on an IDIQ. BLI 8822G01101 is a dedicated procurement line whose program title IS 'Personnel Recovery Support System (PRSS)' and whose narrative owns that exact name, so a device buy is that line's own end item rather than something it merely supports. The only other owner of the name is RDT&E PE 0604601A (Infantry Support Weapons); an indefinite-delivery production buy of fielded devices belongs to the procurement line, not the development PE.

refute_a.reason: The line's narrative says 'The Personnel Recovery Support System (PRSS) consists of several components that included Personnel Reco[very Device]', so the device the IDIQ buys is this dedicated OPA line's own component rather than a platform it supports; a hardware delivery contract is procurement-colored, which fits the procurement line and not the RDT&E alternative, and the BLI is single-program with no rollup character.

refute_b.reason: The only competing owner, 0604601A, is a seven-name Infantry Support Weapons development rollup that carries PRSS without the article, while 8822G01101 is a single-name line whose program title IS PRSS and whose row matches the announcement's 'The Personnel Recovery Support System' verbatim; the Personnel Recovery Device is that program's own end item, not a variant or a contractor name.

proposals.announcement_evidence: cargo platform health environment kits for cargo helicopters
proposals.rationale: The announcement spells out 'cargo platform health environment kits for cargo helicopters', which is the CPHE modification kit for the CH-47. BLI 3264AA0252 (CH-47 Cargo Helicopter Mods, MYP) owns the name 'Cargo Platform Health Environment (CPHE)' in its own narrative, and no other line in this org's index carries that name. A firm-fixed-price buy of CPHE kits is exactly what a cargo-helicopter modifications procurement line funds: the kit, not the airframe, is the item, so this is not a platform the contract merely supports.

refute_a.reason: The procured item is the CPHE kit, not the helicopter: 3264AA0252's narrative is about 'integrating and fielding capability to the remaining fleet with Cargo Platform Health Environment (CPHE) and Improved Vibration Control System (IVCS)', and buying modification kits is exactly what an aircraft-procurement modifications line funds, so the cargo helicopter is the platform the kit goes on while the kit itself is this line's own work.

refute_b.reason: 'Cargo Platform Health Environment (CPHE)' appears exactly once in the 1,439-row index, on 3264AA0252, whose other rows (CH-47F, CAAS, DAFCS, IVCS) confirm the cargo-helicopter airframe the announcement names; the alias is a verbatim four-word match with no alternative owner and no increment ambiguity.

proposals.rationale: '40 mm M320 and 40 mm M320A1 grenade launchers' is the M320 Grenade Launcher Module and its A1 variant; the announcement uses the fielded short form rather than the J-book's 'Grenade Launcher Module' phrasing, which is why the deterministic matcher left it in the residue. A firm-fixed-price buy of the launchers themselves is that procurement line's own end item.

refute_b.reason: 8181G01501 is the only line in the index carrying any grenade-launcher name, and its row 'The M320 Grenade Launcher Module (GLM)' contains the designator 'M320' literally, so the alias is real rather than invented; the M320A1 is the same GLM in its standalone configuration and no separate index line owns an A1 variant.

proposals.announcement_evidence: 40mm M320/M320A1 grenade launchers and non-functional training displays
proposals.rationale: Same item as record 38 under an earlier Capco contract: the award buys M320/M320A1 grenade launchers (plus non-functional training displays of the same launcher) and BLI 8181G01501 (XM320 Grenade Launcher Module) is the only line in this org's index whose narrative owns the M320 GLM name. refute_b.reason: Same sole-owner situation as record 38, and the secondary item offers no rival: 'training display', 'non-functional' and 'nonfunctional' return zero rows across the entire index, so no training-devices line competes for this award's evidence.

proposals.announcement_evidence: to support acquisition of the Terrestrial Layer System Brigade Combat Team
proposals.rationale: TLS-BCT is the brigade-combat-team increment of the Terrestrial Layer System, and the awardee (Lockheed Martin, Liverpool/Syracuse, New York) is the TLS-BCT prime rather than a third-party services house. Three lines own a TLS name: RDT&E PEs 0304270A and 0609277A, and procurement BLI 9546B97600. The obligated money is fiscal 2022 other procurement, Army, which selects the procurement line, and 9546B97600's narrative owns the unqualified name 'Terrestrial Layer Systems (TLS)' (its other row, TLS EAB, is the echelon-above-brigade increment). The residual risk is the announcement's vague verb 'to support acquisition of', which is why the appropriation and the prime's identity carry the weight here.

refute_a.reason: The money color is stated and matches exactly — fiscal 2022 other procurement, Army against 9546B97600, whose lexicon_doc 346 is the Other Procurement, Army book — and the named thing (TLS BCT) is the program itself, not a platform the contract supports; the vague verb 'to support acquisition of' is the residual risk, but OPA dollars to the TLS-BCT prime at its own Syracuse EW facility are not the generic engineering-support or base-operations pattern §3 rejects, and the TLS line is program-specific rather than a catch-all.

refute_b.reason: Wrong increment: 9546B97600 owns exactly two names and the only increment it names is 'Terrestrial Layer System Echelon Above Brigade (TLS EAB)', while 'brigade combat' and 'BCT' return zero rows anywhere in the index, so the announcement's TLS-BCT matches no owned name and the unqualified TLS fallback is owned equally by RDT&E PEs 0304270A and 0609277A.

proposals.announcement_evidence: the Compact Semi-Automatic Sniper Systems and the Squad Designated Marksman Rifle
proposals.rationale: The announcement names the Squad Designated Marksman Rifle explicitly; the CSASS and the SDMR are both the Heckler & Koch G28-derived M110A1, and the awardee is H&K on the M110A1 IDIQ. BLI 3181GZ1500 (Sniper Rifles Modifications) is the only line in this index whose narrative owns 'M110A1 Squad Designated Marksman Rifle (SDMR)', alongside the M110 SASS and MK22 PSR, so the SDMR is an item this line itself funds rather than a platform it supports. The announcement drops the M110A1 prefix the J-book uses, which is why an alias judgement rather than a literal name match is required.

refute_a.reason: Mission mismatch of the §3 platform kind: 3181GZ1500 is 'Sniper Rifles Modifications', and every one of its lexicon rows reads as upgrade content — the narrative names the SDMR only inside 'The current Army fleet of sniper weapons, consisting of the M110 SASS, the M2010 ESR, the M107 LRSR, the MK22 PSR and the M110A1 SDMR, require continuous upgrades to the weapon, components, and…', with its own procured items being the Advanced Sniper Accessory Kit, Ballistic Weather Meter, spotting scope and tripod kits — so the rifles are the fielded fleet this line upgrades, not what it buys, while the announced action is a $33.5M increment on H&K's CSASS production IDIQ for whole rifles; that whole-rifle procurement sits on rifle lines of its own in this same index (8190G01506, 'Precision Sniper Rifle'), and the first-named half of the award, the Compact Semi-Automatic Sniper Systems, is not owned by 3181GZ1500 at all, so an unknown share of the money is another line's work and no appropriation is stated to corroborate.

refute_b.reason: 'Squad Designated Marksman Rifle' is a verbatim substring of 3181GZ1500's row and no other line in the index owns it; CSASS/'Compact' returns no weapons row at all, so the award's second named item has no rival owner either, and the dropped 'M110A1' prefix is the same weapon rather than a different variant.

proposals.announcement_evidence: the low-rate initial production of lightweight command launch units in support of the Javelin Weapon System
proposals.rationale: The announcement names lightweight command launch units, which BLI 0648CC0007 (Javelin (AAWS-M) System Summary) owns verbatim as 'Lightweight Command Launch Units (LWCLU)'. The competing owner is RDT&E PE 0604611A (JAVELIN), which carries the singular form; the obligated money is fiscal 2022 missile procurement, Army, and the work is low-rate initial production, so the procurement line is the one whose own work this action pays for. refute_b.reason: The only rival owner, RDT&E PE 0604611A, carries the singular 'Lightweight Command Launch Unit (LWCLU)' while 0648CC0007 carries the plural form the announcement uses, and the named fiscal 2022 missile procurement funds plus low-rate initial production settle the identity; LWCLU is a single item with no increment split in the index.

proposals.announcement_evidence: the Integrated Fires Mission Command Integrated Battle Command System Development Program
proposals.rationale: The announcement names the Integrated Battle Command System development program and obligates fiscal 2021 RDT&E, Army against Northrop Grumman's long-running IBCS development contract W31P4Q-08-C-0418 at Huntsville. Five lines own an IBCS name; the appropriation eliminates the three procurement lines (8930C61001, 9280BZ5075, 9301H37300), leaving 0605457A (Army Integrated Air and Missile Defense) and 0606118A (AIAMD Software Development & Integration). 0606118A is the later software-only carve-out, while the base IBCS development effort under this 2008 contract sits in the AIAMD development PE, which owns 'Integrated Battle Command System (IBCS)' outright. The two-way RDT&E collision is the weakest point of this proposal and is stated rather than hidden.

refute_b.reason: Five PEs own an IBCS name (0605457A, 0606118A, 8930C61001, 9280BZ5075, 9301H37300, the last byte-identical to the proposed row), and after the RDT&E appropriation the announcement's words still cannot choose between 0605457A and 0606118A, which owns its own IBCS name for AIAMD software development work on the same Northrop development effort.

proposals.rationale: BLI 3484D15501 carries the program title 'Ground Mobility Vehicles (GMV)', which is why this record surfaced, but the only name the line's narrative actually owns is 'The Army Infantry Squad Vehicle (ISV)' — a different vehicle from the SOCOM-derived GMV 1.1 this award buys, on a SOCOM contract number (H92222-13-D-0013). Matching the announcement to the line would mean matching the budget-line title rather than a name the PE owns, and the evidence does not distinguish an interim GMV 1.1 buy from the ISV program of record, so this does not meet the evidence standard.

Four separate lines in this org's index own a Common Bridge Transporter name — 2831MX0100 (Tactical Bridging), 3542MA8890 (Tactical Bridge, Float-Ribbon), 3758G06520 (Bridge Supplemental Set) and 1110MA4500 (Modification Of In-Svc Equipment, OPA-3). proposals.announcement_evidence: technical support for the Utility Helicopters Project Office
proposals.rationale: Rejected under the §3 generic-services pattern.
